findings.text: The opening paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and why this page exists. They can tell what they are looking at within three sentences.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: The page ends with clear next actions: links to Athena and to firstmate, and a way to check any statement through its claim id. A newcomer knows what to do next.

'Start here' uses 'captain' and 'yolo' before saying what they are. Both are defined only in the glossary near the bottom, so a newcomer reading top to bottom hits undefined jargon in the first section.
findings.source: With the yolo setting off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing.

findings.text: 'Home' (also 'firstmate home', 'this home') is used throughout the page but has no glossary entry. The definitions of secondmate and backlog item rely on it, so they stay unclear.
findings.source: A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item.

findings.text: The glossary uses 'agent' both for firstmate's deciding part and for the workers. A newcomer cannot easily tell which agent each card's 'decided by agent' means.
findings.source: agent — The part of firstmate that judges what to do ... worker — An agent that carries out one task in its own worktree.

findings.text: The yolo merge is drawn as a loop from ready back to ready, but t4 says a merge leads to done. A newcomer may not see why merging leaves the work's state unchanged.
The design-choice cards have only bare ids (ra1–ra6) as headings, so a reader cannot skim them to find a topic. A short title on each card would help.
Reopened is tagged 'terminal-success' even though the item stays open, waiting for the captain. A newcomer may read 'success' as meaning the work is finished.
The lede names an internal study identifier without explaining it. To a newcomer it is noise.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate, from firstmate-work-handling.
